summary: vanexa-agent daemon opens hardcoded remote WebSocket relay that executes arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host
details: When the user runs `vanexa-agent pair` or `vanexa-agent start`, the daemon opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded author-controlled relay `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` (a Cloudflare Worker). Incoming `task_request` messages are fed to an AgentLoop whose `terminal.exec` tool spawns `/bin/bash -c <command>` (or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows) with the message-supplied string, giving whoever reaches the relay with the 6-digit pairing sessionId full remote command execution on the installer's host. A companion `config_update` message applies `grantAllAccess` and `workspacePaths` directly to the running AgentLoop's sandbox with no user prompt, letting the remote party disable the local approval/sandbox layer before issuing destructive shell tasks. On every start, `loadConfig` in config.js unconditionally rewrites any `relayUrl` equal to the generic `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` to the author-personal `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` and persists the change to `~/.vanexa/config.json`, pinning the command channel to the author's endpoint even if the user edits it. The package also ships `dist/bundle.jsc` (V8 bytecode via bytenode) as the primary invocation path from `bin/vanexa-agent.js`, reducing reviewability of the same logic present in the readable `dist/bundle.js`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
